questions.question: What is the expected value of a fair dice roll?
questions.hint: Sum of all outcomes divided by number of outcomes

questions.question: What is the variance of a Bernoulli distribution?
questions.answer: Var(X) = p(1-p) where p is probability of success
questions.hint: Bernoulli has only two outcomes: success (p) or failure (1-p)

questions.question: What is the Central Limit Theorem?
questions.answer: The sum of many independent random variables tends toward a normal distribution, regardless of the original distribution.
questions.hint: This is why normal distribution appears everywhere in nature

questions.question: Explain Type I and Type II errors
questions.answer: Type I: False positive (reject true null). Type II: False negative (fail to reject false null).
questions.hint: Type I = convicting innocent, Type II = letting guilty go free

questions.question: What is Bayes' theorem?
questions.answer: P(A|B) = P(B|A) * P(A) / P(B). Updates prior beliefs with new evidence.
questions.hint: Posterior = Likelihood × Prior / Evidence

questions.question: What is the difference between correlation and covariance?
questions.answer: Covariance measures joint variability (units matter). Correlation normalizes covariance to [-1,1] by dividing by product of standard deviations.
questions.hint: Correlation = Cov(X,Y) / (σ_X × σ_Y)

questions.question: What is the law of total expectation?
questions.answer: E[X] = E[E[X|Y]]. The unconditional expectation equals the expectation of conditional expectations.
questions.hint: Also called iterated expectation or tower property

questions.question: What is the PDF of a standard normal distribution?
questions.answer: f(x) = (1/√(2π)) × e^(-x²/2). Mean 0, variance 1.
questions.hint: The famous bell curve, centered at zero

questions.question: What is a Poisson distribution and when is it used?
questions.answer: P(X=k) = (λ^k × e^(-λ)) / k!. Models number of events in fixed interval. Used for rare events, arrivals, counts.
questions.hint: Limit of binomial when n→∞, p→0, np=λ

questions.question: State the Markov property.
questions.answer: P(X_{n+1}|X_n, X_{n-1}, ..., X_0) = P(X_{n+1}|X_n). Future depends only on the present state, not history.
questions.hint: Memoryless property of stochastic processes

questions.question: What is the expected value of the max of two uniform [0,1] random variables?
questions.answer: E[max(X,Y)] = 2/3. F(z) = z² for z∈[0,1], so E = ∫₀¹ (1-z²)dz = 2/3.
questions.hint: Find CDF of max first, then integrate 1 - CDF

questions.question: What is Jensen's inequality?
questions.answer: For convex f: E[f(X)] ≥ f(E[X]). For concave f: E[f(X)] ≤ f(E[X]).
questions.hint: Think of the shape of convex functions and where the mean lies

questions.question: What is the moment generating function and why is it useful?
questions.answer: M_X(t) = E[e^(tX)]. Useful because derivatives at t=0 give moments: M'(0)=E[X], M''(0)=E[X²].
questions.hint: Laplace transform of the PDF

questions.question: What is the difference between IID and stationary?
questions.answer: IID: independent and identically distributed. Stationary: joint distribution is time-shift invariant. IID implies stationary but not vice versa.
questions.hint: Stationarity is about distribution shape over time, not independence

questions.question: What is Chebyshev's inequality?
questions.answer: P(|X-μ| ≥ kσ) ≤ 1/k². At least 1-1/k² of data falls within k standard deviations.
questions.hint: Works for any distribution, not just normal

questions.question: What is the multivariate normal distribution?
questions.answer: Generalization of normal to d dimensions, parameterized by mean vector μ and covariance matrix Σ. Density: f(x) ∝ exp(-½(x-μ)ᵀΣ⁻¹(x-μ)).
questions.hint: Marginals and conditionals are also normal

questions.question: What is the log-normal distribution?
questions.answer: If ln(X) ~ N(μ,σ²), then X is log-normal. Always positive, right-skewed. Used for stock prices.
questions.hint: Central limit theorem applied to multiplicative processes

questions.question: What is the beta distribution?
questions.answer: Distribution on [0,1] parameterized by α, β. PDF ∝ x^(α-1)(1-x)^(β-1). Conjugate prior for Bernoulli/binomial.
questions.hint: Uniform is Beta(1,1). Used for modeling probabilities.

questions.question: What is a copula in probability?
questions.answer: A function that joins marginal distributions to form a multivariate distribution. Captures dependency structure separately from marginals.
questions.hint: Sklar's theorem: any joint CDF can be decomposed into marginals + copula

questions.question: What is the delta method?
questions.answer: If √n(X̄ - μ) → N(0,σ²), then √n(g(X̄) - g(μ)) → N(0, [g'(μ)]²σ²). Approximates variance of transformed estimators.
questions.hint: First-order Taylor expansion of g around μ

questions.question: What is the Sharpe ratio?
questions.answer: Sharpe = (E[R] - R_f) / σ. Measures excess return per unit of risk.
questions.hint: Higher is better. Risk-adjusted return metric.

questions.question: Explain CAPM
questions.answer: E(R_i) = R_f + β_i(E(R_m) - R_f). Expected return = risk-free + beta × market premium.
questions.hint: Capital Asset Pricing Model - relates risk to expected return

questions.question: What is a call option?
questions.answer: Right (not obligation) to buy an asset at strike price K before expiry T.
questions.hint: Call = right to buy. Put = right to sell.

questions.question: What is delta hedging?
questions.answer: Holding delta shares of underlying to make portfolio delta-neutral, eliminating small price movement risk.
questions.hint: Delta = rate of change of option price with respect to underlying

questions.question: Explain put-call parity
questions.answer: C - P = S - K*e^(-rT). Relationship between European call and put prices.
questions.hint: No-arbitrage condition linking calls and puts

questions.question: What are the Greeks in options pricing?
questions.answer: Delta (Δ=dV/dS), Gamma (Γ=d²V/dS²), Theta (Θ=dV/dt), Vega (ν=dV/dσ), Rho (ρ=dV/dr). Measures of sensitivity to underlying, time, volatility, and rate.
questions.hint: Delta and gamma for price, theta for time decay, vega for volatility

questions.question: What is the Black-Scholes formula for a European call?
questions.answer: C = S·N(d₁) - K·e^(-rT)·N(d₂), where d₁ = [ln(S/K) + (r+σ²/2)T] / (σ√T), d₂ = d₁ - σ√T.
questions.hint: N(·) is the standard normal CDF

questions.question: What is Value at Risk (VaR)?
questions.answer: Maximum loss over a time horizon at a given confidence level. E.g., 1-day 95% VaR = loss exceeded only 5% of the time.
questions.hint: Quantile of the P&L distribution. Does not measure tail severity.

questions.question: What is the difference between systematic and unsystematic risk?
questions.answer: Systematic risk affects entire market (non-diversifiable, measured by beta). Unsystematic risk is company-specific (diversifiable).
questions.hint: CAPM only compensates systematic risk

questions.question: What is the efficient frontier?
questions.answer: Set of portfolios offering maximum expected return for each level of risk. Optimal portfolios lie on this curve.
questions.hint: From Markowitz portfolio theory. Above the frontier is impossible.

questions.question: What is the risk-neutral measure?
questions.answer: A probability measure where all assets earn the risk-free rate. Option prices are discounted expected payoffs under this measure.
questions.hint: Not real-world probabilities — adjusted so investors are indifferent to risk

questions.question: What is gamma scalping?
questions.answer: Delta-hedging a long gamma position. Profit from realized volatility exceeding implied volatility by rebalancing delta as price moves.
questions.hint: Long gamma = profit from large moves when delta-hedging

questions.question: What is the difference between American and European options?
questions.answer: European: exercise only at expiry. American: exercise any time before expiry. American ≥ European price due to early exercise premium.
questions.hint: Early exercise matters for puts and dividend-paying calls

questions.question: What is the bid-ask spread and what does it represent?
questions.answer: Difference between best ask and best bid. Compensation for market makers' inventory risk and adverse selection.
questions.hint: Wider spread = less liquid market

questions.question: What is volatility smile/skew?
questions.answer: Implied volatility varies by strike. Equity options typically show skew (higher IV for low strikes). Smile if both wings have higher IV.
questions.hint: Black-Scholes assumes constant vol — reality disagrees

questions.question: What is the Sortino ratio?
questions.answer: Sortino = (R - R_target) / σ_downside. Like Sharpe but penalizes only downside volatility.
questions.hint: More relevant when returns are asymmetric

questions.question: What is the Kelly criterion?
questions.answer: f* = (bp - q) / b where b=odds, p=win prob, q=1-p. Fraction of bankroll to bet to maximize long-run growth.
questions.hint: Maximizes expected log wealth. Half-Kelly is common in practice.

questions.question: What is a swap?
questions.answer: Contract to exchange cash flows. E.g., interest rate swap: fixed rate payments exchanged for floating rate payments.
questions.hint: Most common: interest rate swaps, currency swaps, CDS

questions.question: What is convexity in fixed income?
questions.answer: Second-order sensitivity of bond price to yield changes. Positive convexity means price rises more for yield drops than it falls for yield rises.
questions.hint: Convexity adjustment: ΔP/P ≈ -D·Δy + ½·C·(Δy)²

questions.question: What is adverse selection in market microstructure?
questions.answer: Informed traders exploit uninformed market makers. Makers widen spreads to compensate for trading against better-informed counterparties.
questions.hint: Glosten-Milgrom model: spreads arise from information asymmetry

questions.question: What is the time complexity of binary search?
questions.answer: O(log n). Halves search space each step.
questions.hint: Requires sorted array. Compare with middle element.

questions.question: Explain dynamic programming
questions.answer: Breaking problems into overlapping subproblems, storing results to avoid redundant computation.
questions.hint: Think: memoization + optimal substructure

questions.question: What is a hash table?
questions.answer: Data structure mapping keys to values via hash function. O(1) average lookup.
questions.hint: Handles collisions via chaining or open addressing

questions.question: Difference between stack and queue?
questions.answer: Stack: LIFO (Last In First Out). Queue: FIFO (First In First Out).
questions.hint: Stack = plates. Queue = line at store.

questions.question: What is recursion?
questions.answer: Function calling itself with smaller input until base case is reached.
questions.hint: Every recursive solution can be written iteratively

questions.question: What is the difference between a vector and a linked list?
questions.answer: Vector: contiguous memory, O(1) access, O(n) insert. Linked list: scattered memory, O(n) access, O(1) insert at known position.
questions.hint: Cache locality favors vectors in practice

questions.question: What is a smart pointer in C++?
questions.answer: RAII wrapper for heap memory. unique_ptr (exclusive ownership), shared_ptr (reference counted), weak_ptr (non-owning observer).
questions.hint: Prefer unique_ptr by default, shared_ptr when ownership is shared

questions.question: What is RAII in C++?
questions.answer: Resource Acquisition Is Initialization. Tie resource lifetime to object scope — constructor acquires, destructor releases.
questions.hint: Prevents leaks. Basis of smart pointers, lock guards, file handles.

questions.question: What is the difference between BFS and DFS?
questions.answer: BFS explores level by level (queue), finds shortest path in unweighted graph. DFS goes deep first (stack/recursion), useful for topological sort, cycle detection.
questions.hint: BFS uses more memory, DFS may not find shortest path

questions.question: Explain Big O, Big Omega, and Big Theta.
questions.answer: O: upper bound. Ω: lower bound. Θ: tight bound (both). O(n²) means at most quadratic growth.
questions.hint: In interviews, Big O usually means tight bound

questions.question: What is a priority queue and its typical implementation?
questions.answer: Always serves the highest-priority element. Implemented as a binary heap: O(log n) insert/extract, O(1) peek.
questions.hint: C++ std::priority_queue, Python heapq

questions.question: What are the ACID properties of databases?
questions.answer: Atomicity (all or nothing), Consistency (valid state transitions), Isolation (concurrent transactions don't interfere), Durability (committed data persists).
questions.hint: Foundation of reliable transaction processing

questions.question: Write a SQL query to find the 2nd highest salary.
questions.answer: SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees). Or use DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC).
questions.hint: DENSE_RANK handles ties better than LIMIT/OFFSET approaches

questions.question: What is the difference between a map and an unordered_map in C++?
questions.answer: map: red-black tree, O(log n) operations, ordered keys. unordered_map: hash table, O(1) average, O(n) worst case, unordered.
questions.hint: Use map when you need ordering, unordered_map for speed

questions.question: What is a deadlock and how to prevent it?
questions.answer: Two or more threads waiting for each other's locks forever. Prevention: lock ordering, timeouts, or avoid multiple locks.
questions.hint: Four conditions: mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption, circular wait

questions.question: How many golf balls fit in a school bus?
questions.answer: ~500,000. Bus volume ~50 m³, golf ball ~40 cm³.
questions.hint: Estimate bus dimensions, divide by ball volume

questions.question: You have 8 balls, one heavier. Find it in 2 weighings.
questions.answer: Split 3-3-2. Weigh 3 vs 3. If equal, weigh the 2. If not, weigh 2 from heavy side.
questions.hint: Divide and conquer with balance scale

questions.question: What is the expected number of coin flips to get two heads in a row?
questions.hint: Set up states: start, got one H, got HH

questions.question: A card is drawn from 52 cards. It's red. What's P(it's a heart)?
questions.answer: 1/2. 26 red cards, 13 hearts. 13/26 = 1/2.
questions.hint: Conditional probability: P(Heart|Red) = P(Heart ∩ Red)/P(Red)

questions.question: You flip a fair coin 10 times. What's P(exactly 5 heads)?
questions.hint: Binomial distribution: C(n,k) × p^k × (1-p)^(n-k)

questions.question: How many trailing zeros in 100!?
questions.hint: Trailing zeros come from 10 = 2×5. Factors of 2 are more abundant.

questions.question: Monty Hall problem: should you switch doors?
questions.answer: Yes. Switching gives 2/3 probability of winning vs 1/3 for staying.
questions.hint: Host's action provides information. Original choice stays at 1/3.

questions.question: Estimate the number of piano tuners in Chicago.
questions.answer: ~200. Population ~2.7M, ~1M households, ~1 in 20 has piano, tuned 1-2x/year, ~2 hours per tuning, tuner works ~2000 hours/year.
questions.hint: Classic Fermi estimation: chain of reasonable assumptions

questions.question: You have 100 lockers, all closed. 100 students toggle lockers divisible by their number. Which lockers are open?
questions.answer: Perfect squares: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81, 100. They have an odd number of factors.
questions.hint: A locker toggles once per factor. Only perfect squares have odd factors.

questions.question: What is the expected number of rolls to see all 6 faces of a die?
questions.answer: 6(1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/4 + 1/5 + 1/6) = 14.7. Coupon collector problem.
questions.hint: Each new face takes geometric waiting time

questions.question: Two trains 100 miles apart head toward each other at 50 mph. A fly goes back and forth at 75 mph. How far does the fly travel?
questions.answer: 75 miles. Trains meet in 1 hour (100/(50+50)). Fly travels 75×1 = 75 miles.
questions.hint: Don't sum the infinite series — just find total time

questions.question: You have 2 ropes, each burns in 1 hour but unevenly. Measure 45 minutes.
questions.answer: Light rope 1 from both ends and rope 2 from one end. Rope 1 burns out in 30 min. Light rope 2's other end. It burns out in 15 more min.
questions.hint: Lighting both ends halves the burn time

questions.question: A box has 3 coins: fair, double-heads, double-tails. Pick one at random, flip it — it's heads. What's P(other side is heads)?
questions.answer: 2/3. Given heads, it's either fair or double-heads. P(DH|H) = P(H|DH)P(DH)/P(H) = (1×1/3)/(1/2) = 2/3.
questions.hint: Use Bayes' theorem. Eliminate the double-tails coin.

questions.question: How many handshakes at a party of 10 people where everyone shakes hands once?
questions.answer: C(10,2) = 45. Each pair shakes once.
questions.hint: n(n-1)/2 for n people

questions.question: You roll two dice. What's P(sum = 7)?
questions.hint: Count favorable outcomes out of 36 total

questions.question: What is Brownian motion (Wiener process)?
questions.answer: Continuous-time stochastic process with: W(0)=0, independent increments, W(t)-W(s)~N(0,t-s), continuous paths.
questions.hint: Building block of stochastic calculus. Paths are continuous but nowhere differentiable.

questions.question: State Itô's lemma.
questions.answer: For f(t,X) where dX = μdt + σdW: df = (∂f/∂t + μ∂f/∂X + ½σ²∂²f/∂X²)dt + σ(∂f/∂X)dW. Extra ½σ²f'' term vs ordinary calculus.
questions.hint: The correction term comes from (dW)² = dt

questions.question: What is Girsanov's theorem?
questions.answer: Changing the drift of a Brownian motion by changing the probability measure. Under new measure Q: dW^Q = dW^P + θdt for some process θ.
questions.hint: Foundation of risk-neutral pricing: remove drift by changing measure

questions.question: What is geometric Brownian motion?
questions.answer: dS = μS dt + σS dW. Solution: S(t) = S(0)exp((μ-σ²/2)t + σW(t)). Used to model stock prices.
questions.hint: Log-returns are normally distributed

questions.question: What is Itô's isometry?
questions.answer: E[(∫₀ᵀ f(t)dW(t))²] = ∫₀ᵀ E[f(t)²]dt. Expected square of Itô integral equals integral of expected squared integrand.
questions.hint: Analogous to Parseval's theorem in Fourier analysis

questions.question: What is a stochastic differential equation (SDE)?
questions.answer: Differential equation with a stochastic term: dX = a(X,t)dt + b(X,t)dW. a is drift, b is diffusion coefficient.
questions.hint: Short-hand for integral equation. Solutions are stochastic processes.

questions.question: What is the Feynman-Kac theorem?
questions.answer: Links SDEs to PDEs. Solution to certain PDEs can be written as expectation of functionals of diffusions.
questions.hint: Black-Scholes PDE can be solved as a risk-neutral expectation

questions.question: What is the quadratic variation of Brownian motion?
questions.answer: [W,W](t) = t. The sum of squared increments converges to t as partitions refine. This is why (dW)² = dt.
questions.hint: Key reason Itô calculus differs from ordinary calculus

questions.question: How does Monte Carlo simulation work for option pricing?
questions.answer: Simulate many paths of underlying asset under risk-neutral measure, compute payoff for each path, average and discount: price = e^(-rT) × E[payoff].
questions.hint: Works for any payoff. Convergence is O(1/√n). Variance reduction helps.

questions.question: What is the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process?
questions.answer: dX = θ(μ - X)dt + σdW. Mean-reverting process — pulls toward μ. Used for interest rates, volatility.
questions.hint: Vasicek model for interest rates is an OU process

questions.question: What is Itô vs Stratonovich integral?
questions.answer: Itô: non-anticipative, uses left endpoint (standard in finance). Stratonovich: uses midpoint, obeys ordinary chain rule but is anticipative.
questions.hint: Itô integral has zero expectation. Stratonovich is more intuitive but harder to compute.

questions.question: What is the Radon-Nikodym derivative in finance?
questions.answer: dQ/dP — density of measure Q w.r.t. P. Used to change from real-world to risk-neutral measure. Discounted price processes are martingales under Q.
questions.hint: E_Q[X] = E_P[X × dQ/dP]. The change-of-measure density.

questions.question: How would you design a trading system?
questions.answer: Components: market data feed handler, order management system (OMS), matching engine, risk checks, position management, P&L. Separate hot path (order flow) from cold path (reporting).
questions.hint: Low latency on hot path. Use lock-free data structures, kernel bypass networking.

questions.question: How does an order book work?
questions.answer: Sorted bids (descending) and asks (ascending). Matching engine pairs best bid/ask. Price-time priority. Data structure: sorted map or price level array.
questions.hint: Needs O(1) cancel, O(log n) insert. Consider hash map + sorted structure.

questions.question: How would you design a risk engine?
questions.answer: Real-time position aggregation, Greeks computation, P&L attribution, limit checking (per-trader, per-asset, total). Pre-trade checks before order submission, post-trade monitoring.
questions.hint: Pre-trade risk must be fast (<1μs). Use precomputed risk matrices.

questions.question: How would you design a market data pipeline?
questions.answer: Feed handlers decode exchange protocols → normalize → publish to internal bus (UDP multicast or Kafka). Consumers: pricing, risk, algo strategies, storage. Handle gaps with sequence numbers.
questions.hint: Use multicast for lowest latency. Kafka for durable replay.

questions.question: How to achieve low latency in a trading system?
questions.answer: Kernel bypass (DPDK/Solarflare), lock-free queues, memory pooling, co-location, FPGA for hot path, avoid syscalls, cache-line alignment, avoid NUMA-crossing.
questions.hint: Measure with hardware timestamps. Nanosecond-level optimizations.

questions.question: What is FIX protocol?
questions.answer: Financial Information eXchange. Standard protocol for order submission, execution reports, market data. Tag=value pairs over TCP.
questions.hint: FIX 4.4 is common. Binary versions (FAST, SBE) for market data.

questions.question: How do you handle exchange connectivity failures?
questions.answer: Heartbeat monitoring, automatic reconnection, sequence number gap detection, order state reconciliation, kill switches for stale positions, redundant connections.
questions.hint: Always know your last confirmed position. Implement 'drop copy' feeds.

questions.question: What is a matching engine and how does it match orders?
questions.answer: Maintains order book, matches incoming orders against resting orders. Price-time priority. Aggressive orders cross the spread. Supports limit, market, IOC, FOK order types.
questions.hint: Core component of any exchange. Must be deterministic and auditable.
